approachQuestion.prompt: Return x raised to exponent e modulo 1000000007, with the convention x^0=1 even for x=0. The identities x^(2k)=(x^k)^2 and x^(2k+1)=x*(x^k)^2 may be used. Examples: (3,5) returns 243; (0,0) returns 1; (0,4) returns 0. Choose the method that avoids repeated subproblems and unnecessary retained state.
constraints: 0 ≤ x < 1000000007; 0 ≤ e ≤ 10^18. Fixed-width multiplication followed by remainder takes constant time without overflow.
Return one residue. Comparisons, integer division by two, and parity tests take constant time; no tail-call optimization is available.
Neither a precomputed table nor a constant-time exponentiation primitive is available.

options.text: Recursively compute the half-exponent result once, then square it and multiply by x if needed, using ordinary call frames.
options.feedback: Reusing the half result avoids duplicate work, but an iterative exponent-state update removes the retained call frames.

options.text: Recursively compute the half-exponent twice independently at every level and multiply those results, with the odd correction.
options.feedback: Although numerically correct, it repeatedly expands identical half-problems and can perform work proportional to the enormous exponent.

options.text: When the exponent is odd, square base and halve exponent without multiplying result by the previous base.
options.feedback: For (3,1), this returns the initial result 1 instead of 3.

options.text: Maintain result=1, base=x, exponent=e. While exponent is positive, multiply result by base modulo the modulus when exponent is odd, square base modulo the modulus, and halve exponent using floor division.
options.feedback: The state maintains result times base raised to the remaining exponent equal to the requested residue, and each iteration removes one exponent bit.

feedback.reason: Maintain result*base^remaining congruent to the requested power.
details: Start result=1, base=x, remaining=e. Until remaining is zero, multiply result by base modulo the modulus if remaining is odd, square base modulo the modulus, and replace remaining by floor(remaining/2). Return result. Maintain only these residues and exponent variables.

Maintain result*base^remaining congruent to the requested power. An odd exponent contributes one base factor, then squaring and halving preserve the invariant. Exponent zero returns one without a special multiplication history.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze method-1 as described in the revealed method. Let e be the original exponent. Fixed-width modular arithmetic costs constant time. Count all temporary words, exclude input and returned residue; the analyzed method-1 has no calls, table, copying, or hashing. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair among the options.

feedback.reason: One iteration per exponent bit uses a fixed number of modular residues.
details: There is one loop iteration per significant bit of a positive e and constant work per iteration. The +2 handles e=0 while keeping a nonzero logarithmic bound. Only a fixed number of words is live.
“O(e + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The analyzed method halves its remaining exponent rather than multiplying once per exponent unit.
“O(log(e + 2)) time, O(log(e + 2)) auxiliary space”: Ordinary recursive repeated squaring retains frames; this analyzed target is the iterative version.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The number of exponent bits processed increases as e grows, despite constant storage.

methodReveal.title: Method to analyze
methodReveal.description: Start result=1, base=x, remaining=e. Until remaining is zero, multiply result by base modulo the modulus if remaining is odd, square base modulo the modulus, and replace remaining by floor(remaining/2). Return result. Maintain only these residues and exponent variables.
